rule: a butt screw through the through bar into a tap in the butting end bears its head on the bar's far face round the hole F2 made, where that hole's axis leaves the bar (F2 drills a side hole square to its face); where F2 makes no hole, the screw meeting the side off square, no head is seated and F2's error stands (after the round-3 acceptance, F7)
design: A plain 80 x 80 block, a 40x40 post on its top, an M8 x 110 (dk 13) up through a Ø9 hole into a bush in the post's core: the hole through the block at 100, the head on its bottom face, 100 % of its Ø9-Ø13 annulus. A brace square to the block's side: the hole through the side, the head on the opposite side, 100 %. A brace rising 30° onto the side: F2 refuses the side hole, a connection error, and no head is seated (draft 2.3 seated one at 100 % on the far side, along the end's normal, where the screw's line would have left the block by its bottom at y -29.28). Through a 40x40 rail: the head on its bottom face over the 8.18 opening, 46.05 %, a fit warning
